messages:
maya: Quick follow-up to the RFC: alternative hybrid idea -- keep explicit short writer leases + implement credit-buckets for read residency. Wanted to surface tradeoffs before we pick one.

maya: Credit-buckets = each node keeps a small number of discrete buckets (hot/warm/cold) rather than an unbounded counter. Moves between buckets on access/decay are cheap and have deterministic demote ordering.

trent: Why buckets over continuous credits?

maya: two main reasons:
- bounded state -> simpler coordinator summaries (O(#prefixes * nodes * buckets) tiny),
- deterministic thresholds make demote ordering reproducible and easier to debug.

arjun: Implementation note: slab-allocator already knows hot/warm surfaces due to allocation age. We can expose a hook to map slab hotness->bucket. Adapter should be trivial.

leo: Operationally we'd want per-tenant bucket caps. Large tenants might fill hot bucket and starve others. How do we prevent tenant hogging?

maya: enforce per-tenant quotas per node and tenant-weighted admission into hot/warm. Also add a soft global fair-share that nudges demote when a tenant exceeds cross-node share percentile.

trent: Correctness: writer leases still need to be strict. Proposed: any operation that mutates or opens a long-lived cursor must acquire a short lease (5-15s). Reads only consult bucket state.

trent: Edge: what if a writer holds a lease and then the node gets told to demote (bucket says cold)? We need demote to respect leases.

maya: demote pipeline will consult active leases; if any present we escalate demote to "deferred" and schedule retry. Demote will also return an ETA to coordinator so it can try other nodes.

arjun: For avoiding extra control churn, I like embedding a tiny header: X-Prefix-Bucket: hot|warm|cold on responses. Coordinator can poll aggregated histograms every N seconds (default 5s).

sasha: I'll add a tiny telemetry envelope: per-node counts into the metrics agent. No extra RPCs. Also add demote_aborts and demote_latency histograms.

leo: How do we ensure demote doesn't cause tail p99 blips? If we evict a warm prefix that suddenly gets a spike, reads will SLOW while it populates again.

maya: two mitigations:
- optimistic prefill: when demote moves to cold, it leaves a tiny prefix sketch (TTL 30s) that helps fast-path rehydrate for short spikes.
- staged eviction: evict only slabs not recently accessed; avoid whole-prefix nukes unless memory pressure is high.

trent: Testing plan: we should run a canary with 1% traffic using feature-flagged bucket mode vs baseline. Measure cross-node handoffs, p99 read latency, and demote-abort rate. Also run failure injection where coordinator loses view for 10s.

arjun: I'll prototype the adapter that emits slab->bucket hints and a demote API: POST /prefixs/{id}/demote?stage=soft|compact|evict. Demote returns {ok, eta_ms, pending_leases}.

maya: Good. Migration plan: start with read-only bucket mode behind flag. If metrics look safe, enable staged eviction in week 2 of canary. Then switch on prefill heuristics in week 3.

sasha: Dashboard: show per-prefix bucket distribution, migration flag state, demote stage counts, pending_leases during demote. Alert on sudden spike in rehydrate rate.

leo: Owners? arjun for adapter + API, sasha for telemetry + dashboard, trent for lease-correctness tests and failure-injection scenarios. maya will coordinate the canary.

maya: Decision for now: proceed with a 4-week spike to validate. If experiment decreases handoffs by >=15% with <5% p99 regression, we consider feature rollout path. Otherwise rollback.

trent: ack. I'll draft test matrix and failure injections.

arjun: starting branch today. Will keep API surface minimal.

sasha: will add metrics and basic dashboard panel by EOD.

maya: Thanks all. I'll post a short RFC note with the experiment matrix. :thumbsup:

leo: :+1:
